pages.ja:
黒い巨人に連れられ、少女は城から抜け出した。
それは不可解な逃走だった。
本来、身を守るのなら最高の場所である城から逃げ出し、守りの薄い森へと逃れたのだ。
pages.jaRuby:

それは不可解な逃走だった。
本来、身を守るのなら最高の場所である城から逃げ出し、守りの薄い森へと逃れたのだ。
pages.en:
Led by the black giant, the girl fled the castle.

It was an inexplicable retreat. She fled the castle—the safest place she could have defended herself—and escaped into the forest, where its protection was far thinner.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The girl flees the castle with the black giant.
It is a baffling escape.
She has abandoned her castle, the place designed to offer her the best defense, to run to the forest.

pages.ja:
危険が迫っている。
その、避けられない事実を感知したのは少女の方が早かった。
……“敵”がゆっくりと城に近づいてくる。
それが強大なものと感じ取れるが故に、少女は城の防壁を最大にし、現れるであろう“敵”に備えて巨人を起こした。
黒い鋼体の巨人、バーサーカー。
理性を奪われ、ただ少女の命令に従うだけの破壊の化身。

理性を奪われ、ただ少女の命令に従うだけの破壊の化身。
pages.en:
——Danger was approaching.

The girl was the first to sense that inescapable truth.

…An “enemy” was drawing slowly closer to the castle.

Sensing the immensity of its power, the girl raised the castle's defenses to their limit and woke the giant to meet the “enemy” when it appeared.

The giant with a body of black steel: Berserker.

Reason stripped away, he was destruction incarnate, obeying only the girl's commands.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Danger is approaching.
The girl was the first one to sense the unavoidable fact.
…The “enemy” is approaching the castle.
Because she felt that the enemy is a great one, she maximized the castle’s defense and woke up the giant in anticipation of the enemy.
The giant of steel, Berserker.
Personification of destruction who has his sanity taken away and only obeys the girl.

pages.ja:
その護衛と城の守りがあれば、どのような敵だろうと恐れる事はない。
そう自分に言い聞かせて、少女は堪えきれない不安に蓋をした。
pages.jaRuby:
その護衛と城の守りがあれば、どのような敵だろうと恐れる事はない。
そう自分に言い聞かせて、少女は堪えきれない不安に蓋をした。
pages.en:
With that guardian and the castle's defenses, no enemy could possibly frighten her.

She told herself so, sealing away an anxiety she could no longer bear.
pages.mirrorMoon:
With her bodyguard and the castle’s protection, she has nothing to fear.
She tells herself this, suppressing her unease.

pages.ja:
だが。
敵が間近に迫った時、傍らで巨人は告げた。
逃げろ、と。
理性を奪われ、口を閉ざした筈の狂戦士でさえ、目前に迫った“何か”には勝てないと悟ったのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
だが。
敵が間近に迫った時、傍らで巨人は告げた。
逃げろ、と。
理性を奪われ、口を閉ざした筈の狂戦士でさえ、目前に迫った“何か”には勝てないと悟ったのだ。
pages.en:
But then——

when the enemy drew near, the giant beside her spoke.

Run.

Even the mad warrior who had lost his reason and should have lost his voice understood that he could not defeat the “something” approaching them.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But.
When the enemy drew near, her giant said…
Run.
Even the one with no reason left understood that he could not beat the approaching foe.

pages.ja:
その瞬間、少女は走っていた。
そんな事は判っている。
そんな事は判っていたのだ。
城の外壁に手をかけたソレは、自分たちに太刀打ちできるモノではない。
不吉な影は陽光を背にして広がり続け、それこそ巨大な影になって、易々と外壁を乗り越えた。
pages.jaRuby:

そんな事は判っている。
そんな事は判っていたのだ。
城の外壁に手をかけたソレは、自分たちに太刀打ちできるモノではない。
不吉な影は陽光を背にして広がり続け、それこそ巨大な影になって、易々と外壁を乗り越えた。
pages.en:
The next instant, the girl was running.

She knew.

She had always known.

The thing laying its hand upon the castle wall was not something they could oppose.

With the sunlight at its back, the ominous shadow went on spreading until it became a colossal darkness and passed effortlessly over the outer wall.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The girl started running at that instant.
She knows that.
She already knew that.
The thing that reached the outer wall is not something they can match.
The ominous shadow expands with the sun behind it, and it becomes a great shadow to easily climb over the outer wall.

pages.ja:
負ける。
自分はともかく、バーサーカーはアレには勝てない。
戦えばきっと負けて、バーサーカーは自分のサーヴァントではなくなる。
それが不安の正体だ。
少女は敗北ではなく、自らのサーヴァントを失う事を恐れて城から逃げだした。
pages.jaRuby:
負ける。

pages.en:
——He would lose.

Whatever happened to her, Berserker could not defeat that thing.

If he fought it, he would surely lose—and then Berserker would no longer be her Servant.

That was the true shape of her fear.

The girl fled the castle not because she feared defeat, but because she feared losing her Servant.
pages.mirrorMoon:
They will lose.
With her aside, Berserker cannot beat that thing.
He will lose if he fights it, and Berserker will not be her Servant anymore.
That is the root of her uneasiness.
She ran away from the castle not in fear of her own defeat, but in fear of losing her Servant.

pages.ja:
黒い巨人に抱えられて森を疾走る。
不安は消えず、より重さを増して背中にのしかかってくる。
逃げられない。
この不安、恐怖からは逃げられない、と少女は漠然と悟り
黒い巨人は足を止めた。

pages.en:
Held in the black giant's arms, she hurtles through the forest.

Her anxiety does not fade. It only grows heavier, bearing down upon her back.

——There is no escape.

Dimly, the girl realizes there can be no escape from this anxiety, from this terror——and the black giant stops.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The black giant carries her as they make their way through the forest.
The uneasiness does not go away, but assails her with increased weight.
She cannot get away.
The girl vaguely understands that she cannot get away from this uneasiness and fearand the black giant stops.

pages.ja: 「ほう。賢明じゃな、勝てぬと悟って出てきおったか」
pages.jaRuby: 「ほう。賢明じゃな、勝てぬと悟って出てきおったか」
pages.en: “Oh? A wise decision. You realized you could not win, and so you came out to meet me.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Oh. Such wisdom. You came out because you know you cannot win.”

pages.ja:
目前には枯れ木の如く老いた魔術師。
その傍らには、白い髑髏の面をつけた暗殺者が控えている。
間桐臓硯。
それが故郷の城を出る時に教えられた、同朋の魔術師である事は一目で判った。
pages.jaRuby:
目前には枯れ木の如く老いた魔術師。

間桐臓硯。
それが故郷の城を出る時に教えられた、[ruby text=マキリ char=2]同朋の魔術師である事は一目で判った。
pages.en:
Before them stands a mage withered as a dead tree.

Beside him waits Assassin, his face hidden behind a white skull mask.

Zouken Matou.

She knows him at a glance as the Makiri mage, one of the allied families she was told about before leaving her ancestral castle.
pages.mirrorMoon:
In front of them is a withered magus.
Next to him is Assassin, wearing a white skull mask.
Matou Zouken.
She figures out right away he is the magus of Makiri that she was informed of when she left her home country.

pages.ja:
「
マトウゾウケン。聖杯に選ばれてもいないモノが、マスターの真似事をしているのね」
黒い巨人から降り、少女は老人と対峙する。
その瞳に恐れはない。
少女と巨人が脅威を感じたモノは、間違っても目前の敵ではないのだから。
pages.jaRuby:
「
マトウゾウケン。聖杯に選ばれてもいないモノが、マスターの真似事をしているのね」

少女と巨人が脅威を感じたモノは、間違っても目前の敵ではないのだから。
pages.en:
“——Zouken Matou. Not even chosen by the Holy Grail, yet you pretend to be a Master.”

The girl descends from the black giant and faces the old man.

There is no fear in her eyes.

For neither she nor the giant has mistaken the enemy before them for the thing they fear.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Matou Zouken. So a person that’s not chosen by the Holy Grail is acting like a Master?”
The girl jumps to the ground and confronts the old man.
There is no fear in her eyes.
The enemy before her is not the terrifying one she sensed.

pages.ja: 「ほ。聖杯はマスターなど選ばぬ。聖杯とは受け皿にすぎぬもの。そこに意思があり聖別をするなどと、おぬしまで教会の触れ込みに毒されたか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「ほ。聖杯はマスターなど選ばぬ。聖杯とは受け皿にすぎぬもの。そこに意思があり聖別をするなどと、おぬしまで教会の触れ込みに毒されたか？」
pages.en: “Hoh. The Holy Grail chooses no Master. A grail is merely a vessel. Have even you been poisoned by the Church's proclamations, imagining it possesses a will and consecrates those it selects?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Hah. The Holy Grail does not choose the Masters. The Holy Grail is just a vessel. Are you poisoned by the church, saying that it has a mind and that it consecrates?”

pages.ja:
「…………………………」
愉快げに笑う老人を、少女は冷淡な瞳で見つめる。
……たしかに老人の言う通り、聖杯は選ばない。
マスターは聖杯に選ばれ、サーヴァントは聖杯の力でカタチを与えられ、マスターによって現世に留まる。
その前提は、意図的に歪められて伝わったものだ。
聖杯戦争の目的が逆である事を少女は知っている。

pages.en:
“…………………………”

The girl regards the old man's delighted smile with cold eyes.

…He is right about the vessel. The Holy Grail itself does not choose.

The story everyone is taught says that Masters are chosen by the Grail, that Servants are given form by its power, and that their Masters anchor them in the present world.

But that rule—the premise on which everything rests—has been deliberately distorted in the telling.

The girl knows that the true purpose of this Holy Grail War is the reverse.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“………”
The girl coldly glares at him as he laughs.
…The Holy Grail does not choose, just like the old man says.
Masters are chosen by the Holy Grail, Servants are given form with the Holy Grail’s power, and they stay in this world with the help of the Masters.
The rules are intentionally distorted and spread around.
The girl knows that the purpose of the Holy Grail War is actually the other way around.

pages.ja:
聖杯はただ注がれるだけのもの。
マスターは選ばれるのではなく、ただ儀式の一端として用意されるだけのもの。
そしてサーヴァントとは、ただ門を開ける為だけのもの
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
The Grail is only a thing into which power is poured.

Masters are not chosen, but merely prepared as components of the ritual.

And Servants exist for no purpose but to open the gate——
pages.mirrorMoon:
The Holy Grail is merely something to be filled.
Masters are not chosen, but prepared as part of the ritual.
And Servants are merely tools used to open the gate

pages.ja:
「……ふん。貴方こそ妄念に毒されているんじゃないの、ゾウケン。
器になる聖杯に意思はないけど、マスターを選び出す大聖杯には意思があるわ。もともとこの土地に原型があるからこそ、貴方たちは英霊を呼び出して聖杯を満たそうとした。
ま、当事者である貴方がソレを忘れるぐらいだから、マキリの血は衰退したんでしょうけど」
少女の声は冷たい。
嘲りでしかないそれを、老人は呵々と笑って受け止める。
pages.jaRuby:
「……ふん。貴方こそ妄念に毒されているんじゃないの、ゾウケン。

ま、当事者である貴方がソレを忘れるぐらいだから、マキリの血は衰退したんでしょうけど」
少女の声は冷たい。
[ruby text=あざけ]嘲りでしかないそれを、老人は呵々と笑って受け止める。
pages.en:
“…Hmph. Aren't you the one poisoned by delusion, Zouken?

“The Grail that serves as the vessel has no will, but the Greater Grail that selects the Masters does. It was because the original foundation already existed in this land that you sought to summon Heroic Spirits and fill the Grail.

“——Well, if even you, one of the people responsible, have forgotten that, I suppose the Makiri blood really has declined.”

The girl's voice is cold.

Her words are nothing but scorn, yet the old man greets them with booming laughter.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hah. Aren’t you the one poisoned by delusion, Zouken?
The Holy Grail that becomes the container has no will, but the Great Holy Grail that chooses the Masters does. You people tried to fill the Holy Grail by summoning heroic spirits because the prototype is here, in this land.
Well, I’m sure the Makiri blood declined because you, the person concerned, forgot about such a thing.”
Her voice is cold.
The old man accepts her scorn with a laugh.

pages.ja:
「いやいや、心配には及ばぬ。マキリの衰退もここまでよ。事は成りつつあってな。予定では次の儀式で行う筈じゃったが、今回は駒に恵まれての。ワシの悲願はあと一手で叶おうとしておる」
「そう。なら勝手にすれば？ わたし、貴方に興味はないわ。わたし以外の器なんて気に入らないけど、どうせ失敗するんだし。邪魔はしないから、大人しく地の底に戻ったら？」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“No, no. You need not concern yourself. The decline of the Makiri ends here. My undertaking is nearly complete. I had intended to perform it during the next ritual, but this time I was blessed with exceptional pieces. My dearest wish now lacks only a single move.”

“I see. Then do as you please. I have no interest in you. I dislike the idea of any vessel but myself, but you will fail anyway. I won't interfere, so why don't you crawl quietly back beneath the earth?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, there is no need to worry. Makiri’s decline will end now. The matter is about to be completed. The plan was to take part in the next ritual, but I was blessed with good game pieces. My earnest desire is about to come true.”
“I see. Then do as you wish. I’m not interested in you. I don’t like having vessels besides myself, but you’re going to fail anyway. I won’t bother you, so why don’t you go back to the pit where you belong?”

pages.ja:
「言われるまでもない。この老体に日の光は辛いのでな、事が済めば早々に古巣に戻る。
だが
やはりのう、こうも上手くいきすぎると逆に不安が大きくなる。万が一のため、おぬしの体を貰い受ける。ここで聖杯を押さえておけば、我が悲願は磐石じゃ」

pages.en:
“You need not tell me. Sunlight is trying for this aged body. Once my business is done, I shall return promptly to my old nest.

“But——when events proceed too perfectly, unease grows all the greater. As insurance, I shall take your body. If I secure you—the Grail—here and now, my dearest wish will be assured.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You do not need to tell me. The sunlight is tough on this old body of mine, so I’ll return to my nest once my business is done.
ButI get rather uneasy when things run too smoothly like this. I shall take your body just in case. My dearest wish is virtually complete if I can seize you here.”

pages.ja:
老人に鬼気が灯る。
白い髑髏がゆらりと立ち上がるも、老人の意思に反して動きを止めた。
「
」
見れば判る。
白い面の暗殺者は、少女を守る巨人に気圧されている。
どうあっても自分では倒せない。
攻め込めば、一太刀のもとに両断される
そう確信したがため、暗殺者は動かずにいた。

pages.en:
——A demonic intensity kindles within the old man.

The white skull rises fluidly beside him, only to halt in defiance of his Master's will.

“————”

The reason is plain to see.

The assassin in the white mask is cowed by the giant guarding the girl.

There is no possible way he can defeat him.

If he attacks, a single stroke will cleave him in two——

Convinced of that, Assassin remains where he is.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Hostility lights up in the old man.
The white skull gets up, but stops in contrast to the old man’s wish.
“”
It’s obvious why.
The white-masked assassin is overawed by the giant who’s protecting the girl.
He has no chance to defeat such a foe.
He will be cut in half with one blow if he steps in
The assassin does not move because he is sure of that fact.

「……ふん。主に似て臆病なサーヴァントね。そんなに死ぬのが怖いなら戦わなければいいのに。貴方といいゾウケンといい、そんなに自分の命が大事？」
「
」
答えはない。
髑髏の面は言葉を発せず、代わりに、彼の主が高らかに笑い出す。

」

pages.en:
“…Hmph. A cowardly Servant for a cowardly Master. If dying frightens you so much, you needn't fight at all. You and Zouken both—are your own lives really so precious?”

“————”

There is no answer.

The skull mask speaks no words. Instead, his Master bursts into ringing laughter.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Heh. Your Servant’s a coward, just like his master. He doesn’t have to fight if he’s so scared of dying. Do you two value your lives so much?”
“”
There’s no reply.
Assassin does not speak, but his master laughs in his place.

pages.ja:
「ああ、大事だとも！ 我が望みは不老不死、こやつの望みも永劫に刻まれる自身の名でな。我らは同じ目的の為、こうして邁進しておるという訳だ」
「……正気なの、貴方。聖杯にかける望みが不老不死ですって？」
少女の瞳に嫌悪が宿る。
老人の口元はさらに歪む。
その罵倒。その罵りこそを待っていた、とでも言うかのように。

pages.en:
“Indeed they are! My wish is ageless immortality, and his is that his name be engraved upon eternity. Thus do we strive together toward the same end.”

“…Are you sane? You mean to wish upon the Holy Grail for immortality?”

Disgust enters the girl's eyes.

The old man's mouth twists farther still, as if that very insult—that very contempt—were what he had been waiting to hear.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course I value my life! My wish is immortality. His wish is for his name to remain forever. We struggle on together for our same goal.”
“…Are you mad? You desire the Holy Grail to grant you immortality?”
Hatred shows in the girl’s eyes.
His grin widens still further.
It’s as if he was waiting for that scornful reaction.

その痛み。生きながら崩れ行く苦しみがおぬしにわかるか？」
「……自業自得でしょう。人の体は百年の時間に耐えられない。それを超えようというのだから、代償は必要だわ。それに耐えられないなら消えればいい。苦しいのなら、死ねば楽になるんじゃなくて？」

pages.en:
“Naturally. Look upon this body—this flesh. It loses function with every passing moment and gives off a reek; it melts away from within, and even as we speak, the cells of my brain surrender the knowledge I have amassed.

“——Can you understand that pain? The torment of crumbling while one yet lives?”

“…You brought it upon yourself. The human body cannot endure a hundred years. If you mean to exceed that span, a price must be paid. If you cannot bear it, then vanish. If you suffer so badly, wouldn't death bring you peace?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course. Look at this body.
It rots by the second, reeking of decay, melts my flesh and bones, and my brain deteriorates and loses its knowledge.
It loses its function by the second, reeking of decay, melts from the inside, and my brain cells lose their knowledge.
This pain. Do you understand the pain of rotting alive?”
“…That’s your own fault. A human body cannot endure a hundred years of life. Compensation is needed if you want to surpass that. If it’s painful, you can be at ease if you die.”

pages.en:
“Ka——”

The old body trembles.

The mage's back shakes as if with a fit of coughing. Then——

“Kaka, kakakakaka…! Just as I expected, Einzbern! A thousand years, and still the same creed! You are dolls to the last. You never did draw near to humanity! Kakakakaka…!”

He roars with laughter, as though nothing had ever amused him more.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Ka.”
The old body trembles.
The magus shakes, as if wracked by coughing, and…
“Kaka, kakakakaka…! I thought so, Einzbern! You people have had the same thought processes for a thousand years! You are just a puppet, after all! You will never know what it means to be human! Kakakakaka…!”
He laughs from the bottom of his heart.

「

人の身において、死に勝る無念などない。虫どもの苗床となるこの痛みなど、己が死に比べれば蚊ほどのものでもないわ。
自己の存続こそが苦しみから逃れる唯一の真理。死ねば楽になるなどと、それこそ生きていない証ではないか。
だからこそおぬしは人形にすぎぬのだ。その急造の体ではあと一年と稼動つまい。短命に定められた作り物に、人間の欲望は理解できぬという事だ……！」

pages.en:
“…What did you say?”

“——Fool. Listen well, child of winter.

“For a human being, no despair surpasses death. This pain of serving as a breeding bed for worms is less than a mosquito's sting beside my own extinction.

“The continuation of the self is the one truth by which suffering may be escaped. To claim that death brings peace is proof that you were never alive at all.

“That is why you are no more than a doll. That hastily fashioned body of yours was not built to last even another year. A fabrication doomed to a short life can never understand human desire…!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…What did you say?”
“Fool. Listen closely, daughter of winter.
For people, there is no regret greater than death.
The pain of my rotten flesh becoming the nest for worms is like a pus in my brain compared to death.
The pain of becoming the nest for worms is like a mosquito bite compared to death.
The sole escape from the pain is to keep myself alive. Saying you will be freed from the pain if you die is proof that you are not alive.
That is why you are a mere puppet. Your hurriedly constructed body should not last for another year. A short-lived artificial product cannot understand human
passion…!”
desire…!”

ねえ。貴方、そんなに死にたくないの？」

“——No, I cannot understand you. Even among human beings, you are an aberration. After living so long, you still cannot accept your own span of life. I can only think you have gone mad.

“Tell me. Are you truly so afraid to die?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Right, I don’t understand. You’re an exception even within the humans. You can’t accept your life span even though you’ve lived for that long. I can only think that
you’re crazy.
you’ve gone mad.
Do you want not to die that bad?”

「無論。ワシは死ぬ道理にはいかん。このまま死にたくはない。まだ世に留まり、生を続けなくてはならぬ。だがそれも既に限界。故に崩れぬ体、永劫不滅の器が欲しい。
その為に」
「その為に聖杯を手に入れようというの？ 死が恐ろしいから、聖杯を求めるの？」

その為に」
「その為に聖杯を手に入れようというの？ 死が恐ろしいから、聖杯を求めるの？」
pages.en:
“Of course. I cannot allow myself to die. I do not wish to die as I am. I must remain in this world and continue my life. But I have already reached my limit. Thus do I desire a body that will not decay, an eternal and indestructible vessel.

“——And for that purpose——”

“You mean to obtain the Holy Grail? You seek it because you are afraid of death?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course not. I cannot die. I do not want to die. I have to stay in this world and live on. But I am at my limit. What I need now is a vessel that will last forever without decay.
That is why…”
“That’s why you want to obtain the Holy Grail? You seek the Holy Grail because you’re afraid of death?”

pages.ja:
「カ、死が恐ろしくない人間がいるのかね？
よいか、いかな真理、いかな境地に辿り着こうと無駄なこと。自己の消滅、世界の終焉を克服する事は出来ぬ。
最期に知っておけ。目の前に生き延びる手段があり、手を伸ばせば届くというのなら
何者をも、たとえ世界そのものを犠牲にしても手に入れるのが人間だとな……！」

pages.en:
“Ka. Does any human being not fear death?

“Mark me: whatever truth or exalted state one may attain, it is futile. None can overcome the extinction of the self or the ending of the world.

“Know this before you die. When the means to survive lies before a human being, close enough to grasp——then he will seize it, whatever he must sacrifice, even the world itself…!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hah, is there anyone that does not fear death?
Understand, it matters little what conclusions you come to in your life. You cannot overcome the collapse of your body or the end of the world.
Let this be a lesson to you. If there is a way to prolong your life and if it is within reachhumans are creatures that will obtain it, even at the cost of the world itself…!”

人の強欲は尽きぬもの。
おぬしとて木々の一本一本が寿命を延ばす妙薬とすれば、この森など瞬く間に食らいつくそう。たとえそれが、僅か一日足らずの延命だとしてもな。
己が一日の為に世界の一部を殺していく。
その願望は、この森だけでは飽き足らず世界中の木々を殺す事になろう」

pages.en:
“——Then you would sacrifice every other human being so that you could go on living?”

“Indeed. If that would grant my wish, I would travel the world killing every human being one by one.

“——Human greed knows no end.

“If every tree were a medicine that prolonged your life, you too would devour this forest in the blink of an eye—even if each tree granted you less than a single additional day.

“For one day of your own life, you would kill one piece of the world.

“And that desire would not be sated by this forest. In the end, it would kill every tree on earth.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Then you’re saying you’ll sacrifice everyone else so you can stay alive?”
“Of course. I would gladly kill everyone in the world if that would grant my wish.
There is no end to human greed.
I am sure you will cut down all the trees in this forest if the trees are a medicine to prolong your life. Even if they may only prolong your life for a day.
Killing a part of the world for another day of life.
That desire shall drive you to go kill every tree in this world.”

当然であろう？ もとより、人間とはそのようにしてここまで広がり、育ち、増え、肥満しきった有象無象。
そこに、もはや連鎖すべき法則など成り立たぬ。いずれ破綻するのであれば、ワシ一人が足並みを崩したところで誰にも異論は挟ませぬわ……！」

“And if that act of felling destroyed the world—everyone else along with it—what would it matter to me?

“Is that not only natural? Humanity is a rabble that has spread, grown, multiplied, and fattened itself by doing precisely that.

“No law can bind such creatures together now. If the whole order is bound to collapse eventually, none shall object when I alone break ranks…!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You will not care if the world dies because of your actions.
Isn’t it natural? Throughout history, humanity has expanded, grown, prospered, and nourished in this way.
There is no space for chain reaction now. If humans are going to eventually die off, nobody will care even if I do not act in concert…!”

She speaks in a voice that is not the voice of a girl.

After looking at him in surprise…
“I’m utterly amazed. You lost your way to that extent?”
The girl speaks in a voice not her own.

pages.en:
“…What?”

“Remember. From where did our dearest wish arise—our yearning to reach the miracle?

“For what purpose did we cling to our humanity, seeking to arrive, still in human form, at a place beyond humanity?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Wh… at?”
“Recall where our desire for a miracle came from.
Why we are particular about having human form, and why we are trying to reach an inhuman place while keeping our human form.”
